nodes.title: Adic étale derived category
nodes.statement: Dét,adic(Y,Λ) is the full enhanced subcategory of D(Yv,Λ) on the objects A that are derived I-complete (EnhancedDerivedSheaves:E4/derived-complete-sheaves, on the replete v-topos of Y) and whose derived reduction A⊗ᴸΛΛ/I lies in the discrete étale subcategory Dét(Y,Λ/I). Derived completeness is a property of the complex, not completeness of its individual cohomology sheaves. The coefficient unit is the completed constant object Λ̂ = Rlimₙ Λ/Iⁿ, not the discrete constant Λ-sheaf.
hypotheses: Λ commutative, I-adically complete; I finitely generated by a regular sequence and containing an integer prime to p.
Y a small v-stack over characteristic-p perfectoid spaces.
proofSteps: Use the enhanced v-derived category (E1) of the replete v-topos of Y (repleteness from C0) and the discrete étale essential-image predicate of C2.
Intersect the derived-I-complete object property (E4/derived-complete-sheaves) with the étale-reduction property; inherit morphisms through the native full subcategory.

hypotheses: Λ commutative, I-adically complete; I finitely generated by a regular sequence and containing an integer prime to p.

The support operations require precisely the geometric eligibility conditions just stated.
proofSteps: Use restriction on the v-site, which preserves limits and reduction (ECD §26), for f*; obtain Rf_* and internal RHom at each finite level from C3.

Construct Rf_! on the coherent tower (Λ/Iⁿ)ₙ from S2's enhanced support pushforward for compactifiable maps representable in locally spatial diamonds with locally finite dim.trg (ECD 22.13–22.23), in the eligible class of S0.

Pass to the enhanced limit; obtain right adjoints by presentability and Rf^! from S3. Identify the finite-level right adjoints with scalar extension by E4/perfect-coefficient-change (Remark 26.3); exactness alone is not such an identification.

nodes.title: Adic forms of ECD Theorems 1.8–1.10 and 1.13
nodes.statement: Let Λ, I be as in L0 and use the completed tensor product and the operations of L0/six-operations-for-adic-coefficients. For a map f : Y → X of small v-stacks: (1.8) f*A⊗̂f*B ≅ f*(A⊗̂B); Rf_*RHom(f*A,B) ≅ RHom(A,Rf_*B); and, for f compactifiable, representable in locally spatial diamonds with locally dim.trg f < ∞, Rf_!(A⊗̂f*B) ≅ Rf_!A⊗̂B for A on Y and B on X, RHom(Rf_!A,B) ≅ Rf_*RHom(A,Rf^!B), and Rf^!RHom(A,B) ≅ RHom(f*A,Rf^!B). (1.9) For a cartesian square with g : X′ → X: g*Rf_*A ≅ Rf′_*g̃*A for qcqs f and A whose reduction modulo I is bounded below; g*Rf_!A ≅ Rf′_!g̃*A and Rg^!Rf_*A ≅ Rf′_*Rg̃^!A under the eligibility hypotheses of ECD 1.9(ii),(iii). (1.13) Pullback along the changes of algebraically closed base field of ECD Theorem 19.5 is fully faithful on Dét(−,Λ). (1.10) If moreover Λ/I is ℓ-power torsion for a prime ℓ ≠ p and f is ℓ-cohomologically smooth, then Rf^!A ≅ f*A⊗̂Rf^!Λ̂ with Rf^!Λ̂ v-locally isomorphic to Λ̂[n], f*RHom(A,B) ≅ RHom(f*A,f*B), and the smooth base-change identities of ECD 1.10(iii) hold. The maps are the canonical ones, and the geometric hypotheses on f and g are those of the discrete theorems.
hypotheses: Λ commutative, I-adically complete; I finitely generated by a regular sequence and containing an integer prime to p.
For (1.10): Λ/I killed by a power of a prime ℓ ≠ p.
Theorem 1.8(iii) is used in the corrected form with A on the source and B on the target (sourceIssue E9).
proofSteps: Each assertion says that a canonical natural transformation between composites of the L0 operations is an equivalence (for 1.13, that a unit is an equivalence).

By Remark 26.3 (L0/reduction-detects-equivalences) every operation commutes with derived reduction modulo I, so the transformation is an equivalence exactly when it is one after replacing Λ by Λ/I, which is killed by an integer prime to p.

For Λ/I apply the discrete theorems: 1.8(i),(ii) and 1.9(i) (Proposition 17.6) from C3; 1.8(iii)–(v) and 1.9(ii) (22.19, 22.23) from S2; 1.9(iii) and 1.10 (23.12, 23.16) from S4; Rf^! and 23.3 from S3; 1.13 (Theorem 19.5) from C6.
For 1.10, Rf^!Λ̂ = Rlimₙ Rf^!(Λ/Iⁿ) is invertible because each Rf^!(Λ/Iⁿ) is v-locally Λ/Iⁿ[n] with n independent of the level (S4).

nodes.title: Characteristic-p scheme v-sheaf
nodes.statement: For a characteristic-p scheme X, construct X◇ as the small v-sheaf on Perf sending S to the maps S → Xad of adic spaces, where Spec R has adic avatar Spa(R,R⁺) for the discrete ring R with R⁺ the integral closure of Fp in R, glued along scheme opens. For affinoid S and X = Spec R, X◇(S) = Hom(R, O(S)): the image of R⁺ lies in O⁺(S) automatically, since O⁺(S) is integrally closed in O(S) and contains Fp. The functor factors through perfection. No finite-type hypothesis is imposed.
hypotheses: X arbitrary of characteristic p.
Universe and smallness conventions of the v-stack supplier.
proofSteps: Affine case: X◇(S) = Hom(R, O(S)) is a v-sheaf because O is (DiamondsAndVStacks:D2/v-descent-of-functions); the plus ring is automatic, matching TauCeti.ValuationSpectrum.spa_integralClosure (Spa(R,R⁺) = Spa(R, image of Fp)).

Smallness: for a perfectoid field K of characteristic p, X◇ ×_{Spd Fp} Spd K is the diamond of the analytification of X_K (AdicSpacesPartII:R1/analytification-universal-property with D6/gluing-and-the-diamond-functor; for X not locally of finite type use infinite-dimensional balls as in the proof of ECD 27.2), and Spd K → * is a v-surjection, so X◇ admits a surjection from a diamond and is small (D4/small-v-sheaves-and-small-v-stacks).

Glue along scheme open immersions, which give open subfunctors. Frobenius is an automorphism of O(S) on perfectoid S (PerfectoidSpaces:P1/characteristic-p-perfectoid-iff-perfect), so X◇ factors through the perfection.

nodes.title: Mixed-characteristic scheme diamond
nodes.statement: Fix a complete DVR O with perfect residue field k of characteristic p. For X locally of finite type over O, X◇(S) is the set of pairs of an untilt S♯ over Spa(O,O) and a map S♯ → X of locally ringed spaces over Spec O. This is a small v-sheaf over Spd O, functorial in X, and X◇ → Spd O is representable in locally spatial diamonds: its base change along a perfectoid S → Spd O is the diamond of the relative analytification X ×_{Spec O} S♯. X◇ itself need not be a diamond: (Spec O)◇ = Spd O. For Spec k it gives Spd(k,k), which differs from the characteristic-p convention when k⁺ ≠ k.
hypotheses: O and X as stated; perfectoid tests S have characteristic p.
proofSteps: Untilts over the explicit pair (O,O) with their marking (PerfectoidSpaces:P1/marked-untilt) satisfy v-descent (DiamondsAndVStacks:D6/untilt-descent-along-v-covers); for affine X = Spec A the condition on S♯ is an O-algebra map A → O(S♯), a v-sheaf condition by D2/v-descent-of-functions.

Base change along a perfectoid S → Spd O: for X closed in affine space over O, maps T♯ → X over S♯ are the points of the closed analytic subspace of the relative affine space over S♯ (an increasing union of relative balls, sousperfectoid and so sheafy) cut out by the equations of X; glue over affine charts. This analytic adic space has locally spatial diamond (DiamondsAndVStacks:D6/etale-site-comparison, ECD Lemma 15.6), so X◇ → Spd O is representable in locally spatial diamonds. Huber's fibre product (AdicSpacesPartII:R1) is not used here: S♯ need not satisfy its noetherian condition.
Glue finite-type affine charts; the local finite-type hypothesis is used for representability.

In a strictly henselian chart with r boundary parameters, R^q j_*Λ is the q-th exterior power of the r Kummer classes Λ(−1), on both sides; the comparison matches generators, cup products and residues, not only ranks. In equal characteristic K = k((t)) is imperfect: de Jong's alteration over K is smooth only over a finite extension K₁ of K (dJ96 Remark 4.2), and purely inseparable extensions change neither étale sites nor diamonds.

nodes.statement: For a separated finite-type f:Y→X with X qcqs, a compactification is a scheme Ybar, a quasi-compact open immersion j:Y→Ybar, a proper p:Ybar→X and the equality p∘j=f. Density is NOT part of the definition: additional proper components are permitted. It is native Scheme and native proper/open predicates.
hypotheses: X qcqs; f separated of finite type (Stacks Section 38.32; BP §2.1.1 takes a noetherian affine base).
The open immersion j is automatically quasi-compact (Y quasi-compact, Ybar quasi-separated over X); the carrier records it as a field.
proofSteps: Bundle the stated native morphisms and factorisation equality.
Define schematic density only as the native separate IsSchemeTheoreticallyDominant j property.

sources.locator: Definition 2.1.2, p. 7; Stacks Tag 0ATT for the general base
sources.match: BP Definition 2.1.2 (S noetherian affine): a compactification is a proper S-scheme with an open immersion of X; no density is required.

acceptance: Extra proper boundary components are allowed; tests must distinguish them from the dense refinement.

nodes.title: Maps and strict maps of compactifications
nodes.statement: A morphism C′→C is an X-map g:Ybar′→Ybar with g∘j′=j. It is strict precisely if the inverse image of j(Y) equals j′(Y), equivalently the open square with the identity of Y is cartesian. Morphisms are not required to be strict in the ambient category.
hypotheses: Two compactifications of the same f.
proofSteps: Bundle the ambient native morphism and two triangle equalities.
Use equality of inverse-image opens as the strictness predicate; equivalent cartesian formulation via open immersions.

sources.match: Zavyalov Definition 2.1.1: morphisms g with g∘j′ = j, strict when g⁻¹(j(X)) = j′(X); Remark 2.1.3: pullback preserves strict morphisms.

acceptance: Keep the direction C′→C: refinements point towards coarser compactifications.

nodes.title: Category of compactifications
nodes.statement: Ordinary compactifications of f, with the morphisms just defined, form a category Comp(f); fp compactifications form the full subcategory Compfp(f). Arbitrary base change induces functors on both categories and preserves strict arrows. Dense and bundle-extending compactifications are full subcategories, with cofinality expressed as initiality towards Comp(f).
hypotheses: Fix f:Y→X; use universe choices consistent with native Schemes.
proofSteps: Compose and take identities on native ambient maps; triangle equations follow by associativity.
Use full subcategories for fp/dense predicates, retaining all ordinary arrows.
Define base change by native pullback and prove coherence; no quotient of isomorphism classes replaces the category.

acceptance: Ordinary category retains parallel arrows for the equaliser test.

nodes.title: Strictness from a dense source
nodes.statement: A map C′→C whose source open j′(Y) is topologically dense in Ybar′ is strict. Over nonreduced schemes topological density still suffices for this set/open equality; schematic density is a separate requirement for vector-bundle extension.
hypotheses: Both are compactifications; the source ambient Ybar′ is separated over X (it is proper), which makes the section closed.
proofSteps: Restrict to the inverse image of the target open: it has a section Y→g⁻¹(Y).
Ybar′ → X is separated, so g⁻¹(j(Y)) → Y is separated and the section j′ is a closed immersion; its image is also open and topologically dense, so it is all of g⁻¹(j(Y)).

sources.match: BP Lemma 2.1.4 and proof: a map from a compactification in which X is dense is strict, because the section of the separated map ξ⋆X → X is a closed immersion with open dense image.
Stacks states the same strictness criterion over any qcqs base; its proof passes to the scheme-theoretic closure, which does not change the underlying space.

acceptance: Do not strengthen density gratuitously; do not use this lemma to satisfy Tag 0ESN.

nodes.title: Cofiltered compactifications
nodes.statement: If f is compactifiable, Comp(f) is cofiltered: it is nonempty, two objects admit a common refinement, and every parallel pair is equalised by a refinement. Dense and schematically dense compactifications form an initial full subcategory; the necessary refinement maps can be strict.
hypotheses: X qcqs and f separated finite type, or simply assume a compactification exists.
proofSteps: Use the native schematic image of Y in the product of two compactifications for a common refinement.
For a,b:C′→C, pull back the closed diagonal of separated C over X to obtain a closed equaliser E⊂C′ containing Y openly; E→X is proper.
Replace by the schematic closure of Y when a strict dense refinement is required.
Prove initiality using nonemptiness and cofilteredness of the relevant comma categories; binary cones alone do not establish it.

sources.match: Stacks Lemma 38.32.1 and proof: the category of compactifications is cofiltered (nonempty, a common refinement by the scheme-theoretic image in the product, the equaliser of two morphisms), the dense and scheme-theoretically dense compactifications are initial, and density gives strictness.

acceptance: Exercise with distinct parallel maps from an extra proper component must be equalised.
This ordinary equaliser is not asserted fp over a noncoherent base.

nodes.title: Compactifications over inverse limits
nodes.statement: For a directed inverse system of qcqs Yi with affine transitions and a least base index 0, and separated finitely presented X0→Y0, the natural functor colimᵢ Compfp(X0×Y0 Yi/Yi)→Compfp(X0×Y0 Y/Y) is an equivalence. It sends strict arrows to strict arrows, and a strict arrow at the limit is strict after increasing the index.
hypotheses: Y=lim Yi, all relative objects fp.
proofSteps: Descend ambient fp schemes and maps using relative diagram descent.
Descend properness, open immersions and their factorisation identities.

For strictness descend the equality of the two quasi-compact opens g⁻¹(j(Y)) and j′(Y) with AlgebraicGeometry.exists_map_preimage_eq_map_preimage (Stacks 01Z4(2)), applied to the diagram of descended ambient compactifications.
Use eventual equality for full faithfulness, not a set-level object bijection.

sources.match: Zavyalov Lemma 2.1.4: for a directed system of qcqs schemes with affine transitions and a smallest index, colim_I Comp_fp(X₀×Y_i/Y_i) → Comp_fp(X₀×Y/Y) is an equivalence; the proof cites Stacks 01ZM, 0EUU and 081F.

acceptance: Both object and arrow descent, including relations, are required.

nodes.title: Strict cofilteredness of fp compactifications
nodes.statement: For X qcqs and separated finitely presented f:Y→X, Compfp(f) is nonempty; any two objects admit an fp common refinement with strict arrows, and any parallel pair is equalised by a strict arrow from an fp compactification.
hypotheses: No noetherianity of X required.
proofSteps: Choose a noetherian approximation of X and descend f and the finite diagram of compactifications using the fp limit equivalence.
At the noetherian stage use Nagata and the full cofilteredness/equaliser proof; closed subschemes of finite-type noetherian ambients are fp.
Take the schematic closure to obtain strict arrows, then base change and use preservation of strictness.

sources.match: Zavyalov Corollary 2.1.5: Comp_fp(X/Y) is nonempty, has strict common refinements and strict equalising morphisms; the proof uses noetherian approximation, Lemma 2.1.4, Remark 2.1.3 and Stacks 0ATU at a noetherian stage.

acceptance: Avoid using a potentially non-fp equaliser directly over the original noncoherent base.

nodes.title: Cartier-boundary compactifications
nodes.statement: Over a noetherian affine base S, for separated finite-type Y→S, compactifications whose complement supports an effective Cartier divisor form an initial full subcategory of Comp(f). Refinements to arbitrary compactifications may be chosen strict. The empty boundary is permitted as the empty effective Cartier divisor.
hypotheses: Noetherian affine S, as in BP §2.1.1.
proofSteps: Take a coherent ideal I of Ybar with V(I) = Ybar \ Y, for instance the reduced boundary.

Blow up Ybar (not Y) at I; the centre is disjoint from Y. The blow-up is proper, an isomorphism over Y, and the inverse image of I is an invertible ideal (tauceti:TauCetiRoadmap/StableReduction layer 4), so the new boundary is an effective Cartier divisor.

The complement of an effective Cartier divisor is scheme-theoretically dense, so Y is dense in the blow-up and the refinement map is strict (L2/strict-from-dense); a preliminary passage to the scheme-theoretic closure is harmless but not needed.
Combine with cofilteredness to prove initiality, not only existence of a dominating object.

sources.match: BP Lemma 2.1.5 and proof: blowing up the reduced boundary ideal gives cofinal compactifications with Cartier boundary and strict maps; the printed proof blows up X where X̄ is meant (sourceIssue E2).

acceptance: Blow-up is the identity on Y.
Does not import flattening through L5, which would make a cycle.

nodes.title: Vector-bundle extension compactifications
nodes.statement: Under BP §2.1.1 hypotheses, for finite locally free F on Y, compactifications to which F extends as finite locally free form an initial full subcategory. Strict refinements exist to each compactification. Rank is locally constant and may differ on different open-and-closed rank pieces.
hypotheses: S noetherian affine; Y finite type separated; F finite locally free, not necessarily constant rank.
proofSteps: Decompose Y into its finitely many open-and-closed constant-rank pieces Y_r; take the disjoint union of their scheme-theoretic closures in the given ambient. This is proper over S, strict over Y, and each Y_r is scheme-theoretically dense in its closure.
Extend F|Y_r to a coherent (finitely presented) module on its closure (SF.0, Stacks 0G41).

On each closure apply Stacks Lemma 31.36.3 (Tag 0ESN): the blow-up in the r-th Fitting ideal is Y_r-admissible and the strict transform is locally free of rank r. The blow-up is from Tau Ceti StableReduction layer 4; the Fitting-ideal algebra is AdicSpacesPartII:R2/fitting-ideal-invertible-locally-free; the module strict-transform argument of Tag 0ESN is carried out in this node.
Combine the locally free strict transforms; use cofilteredness, persistence under pullback and dense strict refinements to prove initiality.

sources.locator: Lemma 2.1.6, p. 7, corrected using Stacks Tag 0ESN
sources.match: BP Lemma 2.1.6 and proof: a coherent extension (Tag 0G41) followed by a blow-up making the strict transform locally free (Tag 0ESN); the density and constant-rank hypotheses of Tag 0ESN are not arranged in the printed proof (sourceIssue E1).
Apply only after the schematic-density and constant-rank repair; imports generic blow-ups.
Extension of a finite-presentation quasi-coherent module; under noetherian hypotheses this is coherent. Supplier SF.0 owns it.

acceptance: Test rank one on one connected component and rank two on another.
Schematic density and constant rank must be checked BEFORE applying Tag 0ESN.

nodes.title: Higher étale cohomology continuity
nodes.statement: Let Xi be a directed inverse system of qcqs schemes with affine transitions and limit X. For a compatible system of abelian étale sheaves Fi with transition maps, set F=colimᵢ πi⁻¹Fi. Then colimᵢ Hqét(Xi,Fi)≅Hqét(X,F) for every q≥0. A sheaf descended from a fixed stage is a special case. For the system Gm,Xi, the sheaf colimit is Gm,X by its finite-presentation representing scheme; the inverse-image maps πi⁻¹Gm,Xi→Gm,X need NOT be individually isomorphisms.
hypotheses: qcqs stages, affine transitions; sheaf transition maps with their composition law.
proofSteps: Identify the limit étale site through finitely presented étale objects, eventual equality and descended finite covering families.
Apply the étale-topos continuity theorem to F=colim πi⁻¹Fi for all q.
For Gm, descend a unit and its inverse on each fp étale chart; this identifies the SHEAF COLIMIT with Gm,X, not the individual inverse image. Apply the same Hq theorem, as in CES §4.10.

sources.match: Stacks Theorem 59.51.3: for a directed system of qcqs schemes with affine transitions and a compatible system of abelian sheaves, colim_i H^p(X_i,F_i) = H^p(X, colim f_i^{-1}F_i) for every p ≥ 0.

sources.locator: §4.10, especially (4.10.5)–(4.10.7), printed pp. 9–11 in the retrieved PDF
sources.match: Česnavičius §4.10 applies this continuity ([SGA 4, VII, 5.9]) to finite étale group schemes, and §§5.3–5.4 to G_m; it is a consumer of the theorem, not its proof.

acceptance: Include all q, including q=2 for Gm.
Do not substitute ordinary ring/global-section continuity.

nodes.title: Continuity of constructible derived Hom
nodes.statement: For a small filtered affine-transition system of qcqs schemes Xα with limit X and a Noetherian ring Λ, let Fα0∈D−c(Xα0,Λ), Gα0∈D+(Xα0,Λ). Then colimα Hom(Fα,Gα)→Hom(F,G) is an isomorphism, likewise after shifts. The lemma itself imposes no invertibility or noetherianity on the schemes.
hypotheses: Uniform upper bound on F and lower bound on G inherited from the fixed stage.
proofSteps: Truncate the fixed-stage bounded-above F against bounded-below G and induct on its finite cohomological range.
For a constructible sheaf F, use an exact sequence K→j!ΛU→F→0 with U→Xα0 qc étale and K constructible; induct on Ext degree.
For F=j!ΛU, apply adjunction and étale higher-cohomology continuity.

sources.locator: §1.4 continuity lemma proof, pp. 4–5 (unnumbered lemma; Hom is a stronger claim in its proof)
sources.match: The Hom statement is proved explicitly for F∈D−c and G∈D+, inside the proof of the unnumbered lemma. No invented numbering (i)/(ii).

acceptance: Record asymmetric D−c and D+ hypotheses, not two arbitrary unbounded complexes.

nodes.title: Continuity of bounded constructible categories
nodes.statement: For a small filtered affine-transition system of qcqs schemes Xα with limit X and a Noetherian ring Λ, the natural functor 2-colimα Dᵇc(Xα,Λ)→Dᵇc(X,Λ) is an equivalence. Bounded constructible complexes, maps and finite diagrams descend, and equality is eventual. No invertibility assumption is in the lemma; no enhanced unbounded equivalence is asserted.
hypotheses: qcqs schemes with affine transition maps over a small filtered index category; a fixed noetherian coefficient ring Λ. No invertibility of any integer on the schemes is assumed (ABE §1.4 lemma).
proofSteps: Use the preceding Hom theorem for full faithfulness.
Descend a finite constructible stratification and finite locally constant sheaves using finitely presented étale data.
Reconstruct bounded complexes by descending extension classes through Hom continuity, then descend finite diagram relations.

sources.locator: §1.4, unnumbered continuity lemma and proof, pp. 4–5

This owns the ABE-25/A11 input requested by GeneralBasesFourier.

nodes.title: Proper-support operations over qcqs schemes
nodes.statement: Extend the EXISTING scheme étale proper-support carrier to separated finite-type maps between qcqs schemes: for a compactification f=p∘j, Rf!=Rp*j!. On the supplied enhanced left-completed torsion category with n invertible, use coherent compactification independence; regular adic coefficients use the enhanced inverse limit. Provide the composition, arbitrary base-change and projection-formula identifications with the classical noetherian formalism. Perfections in characteristic p use universal-homeomorphism invariance.
hypotheses: The noetherian six-operation carrier and proper base-change/finite-cd inputs are supplied by SF.2.
No new Rf! carrier is defined in parallel with that supplier.
proofSteps: Use nonnoetherian Nagata and full cofilteredness for compactification choices.

Descend finite-presentation proper/open diagrams and finite constructible coefficients to noetherian models; extend the imported noetherian proper base-change map by L2 cohomology/constructible continuity. Pass to larger torsion modules and left-completed complexes only with the coefficient/bound proof recorded in G-support. Compare Rp*j! on strict refinements.
Use coherent enhanced descent over the compactification category, including composition and base-change diagrams.

For regular adic coefficients apply E4/coefficient-system-reconstruction on the replete pro-étale topos (repleteness from SF.2) levelwise; for perfections use topological invariance of the étale site (SF.0).

sources.match: Proof of 27.4: by Nagata f factors as an open immersion followed by a proper map, any two factorizations are dominated by a third (the category of factorizations is filtered), and this makes Rf_! = Rp_* j_! essentially independent of the choice.

nodes.title: Comparison of residue-field conventions
nodes.statement: For a perfect field k over Fp with k⁺ the integral closure of Fp, the inclusion k⁺⊂k gives a natural map Spd(k,k)→Spd(k,k⁺) between the mixed-characteristic residue avatar and the characteristic-p scheme avatar. In the finite algebraic extension case k=k⁺ it is the identity. It is not asserted to be an isomorphism for general k.
hypotheses: O has residue field k; k perfect.
proofSteps: Use the identity ring map and the inclusion of plus rings in native Spa.
Use native spa_antitone and v-sheafification to get the direction.
For k algebraic over Fp all elements are integral, so the pairs agree.

nodes.title: Tensor and pullback compatibility
nodes.statement: The scheme comparison cX* is symmetric monoidal for the discrete derived tensor and for the adic completed derived tensor. For every characteristic-p scheme map f:Y→X the canonical natural transformation (f◇)*cX*≃cY*f* is an equivalence. The mixed-characteristic version satisfies the same identities in its finite-type/local finite-type construction range.
hypotheses: Use each comparison functor with its specified coefficient carrier; f* exists without support eligibility.
proofSteps: Compute restriction on the underlying site maps.
For adic coefficients compare the completed tensor by reduction and use L0 detection.
Check the identity/composition coherence inherited from morphisms of sites.

nodes.title: Analytic test space over a DVR
nodes.statement: For O as in L1, give O[[x]] the (π,x)-adic topology, set T=D(x)⊂Spa(O[[x]],O[[x]]), and use the structural T→Spa(O,O). T is analytic. Its diamond is surjective and ℓ-cohomologically smooth over Spd O for ℓ≠p; hence pullback along T◇ is conservative and remains so after base change. For X locally finite type over O, (X×Spec O T)◇≃X◇×Spd O T◇. Spd O is not analytic, so ECD 24.4 is applied only after base change to perfectoid test objects (sourceIssue E4).
hypotheses: Fix a uniformiser π; completion and topology are part of the construction.

nodes.statement: For finite prime-to-p Λ, form a proper hypercover of a finite-type scheme pair by recursively applying the SF.4 alterations to matching objects. An alteration of degree divisible by ℓ is allowed: no trace splitting is used.

Induct on chart dimension; identify the support of the cone as finitely many closed-fibre points (the most singular points).
Proper pushforward is conservative on a complex supported on finitely many closed points: after a finite residue-field extension their stalks appear as a finite direct sum.
L4's proper comparison reduces the pushforward to the trait comparison L6/trait-open-comparison.

At a geometric closed point sbar its two stalks identify canonically with RΓ(IK,M), IK=Gal(Ksep/Ksh), with the residual Gk action; at geometric generic points both give M. These identifications intertwine the comparison, transition maps and twists.

Diamond side: identify the étale site of Spd K with that of Spa K (D6/etale-site-comparison) and v-cohomology with étale cohomology on D_ét (C2); the punctured-trait computation at the closed point and its agreement with the canonical comparison are this node's own work (G-trait).
